#> see '?methods' for accessing help and source code

Source: R documentation: showMethods

Classes and generics are objects too, stored in the environment where they were defined under hidden names. The R Internals manual says the class definition is kept in an object named .__C__ followed by the class name, and the methods of each generic in a "methods table" named .__T__ followed by the generic and its package, which is why neither shows in ls() without all.names = TRUE. The listing of the script shows both kinds, for the classes of the model and for the generics it extended (show:methods, length:base, summary:base, toupper:base).

# Classes and method tables are objects with hidden names in the environment
# where they were defined (R Internals: S4 classes and S4 methods).
grep("^[.]__", ls(all.names = TRUE), value = TRUE)
#>  [1] ".__C__AudioBook"                 ".__C__book"
#>  [3] ".__C__Book"                      ".__C__ebook"
#>  [5] ".__C__Item"                      ".__C__Shelf"
#>  [7] ".__T__[[:base"                   ".__T__coerce:methods"
#>  [9] ".__T__Compare:methods"           ".__T__initialize:methods"
#> [11] ".__T__isbn:.GlobalEnv"           ".__T__isbn<-:.GlobalEnv"
#> [13] ".__T__length:base"               ".__T__matches:.GlobalEnv"
#> [15] ".__T__pages_per_year:.GlobalEnv" ".__T__pair:.GlobalEnv"
#> [17] ".__T__show:methods"              ".__T__summary:base"
#> [19] ".__T__Summary:base"              ".__T__title_of:.GlobalEnv"
#> [21] ".__T__toupper:base"

Source: R Internals: S4 classes

Debugging S4 methods

The R FAQ answer to "How can I debug S4 methods?" is trace() with signature=: the tracer is inserted in the method that will be dispatched for that signature. trace() accepts an expression or function to run on entry (tracer), prints the call unless print = FALSE, and untrace() with the same signature removes it. The NEWS of R 4.5.0 adds that debug() and debugonce() also accept a string naming an S4 generic, and fixes debugonce() with a signature= for a method with a simple body. The general debugging tools are in Debugging.

# FAQ 8.5: trace() with signature= instruments the method that dispatch picks.
trace(
  "pages_per_year", signature = "Book",
  tracer = quote(cat("entering the Book method\n")), print = FALSE
)
#> [1] "pages_per_year"
pages_per_year(Book("Loud Roofs", year = 2021, pages = 198))
#> entering the Book method
#> [1] 39.6
untrace("pages_per_year", signature = "Book")
pages_per_year(Book("Loud Roofs", year = 2021, pages = 198))
#> [1] 39.6

Source: R FAQ 8.5: How can I debug S4 methods?

Last, removing methods and classes is possible and useful in a long interactive session, but it is not something a package does. The last chunk removes a method (a later call on a pair that depended on it fails with the dispatch error), repeats the removal to show the warning, and removes the Shelf class.

# Removing a method (and a class) is possible, mostly useful while developing.
removeMethod("matches", signature("Book", "ANY"))
#> [1] TRUE
msg(matches(lamp, 1L))
#> [1] "unable to find an inherited method for function ‘matches’ for signature ‘x = \"Book\", y = \"integer\"’"
withCallingHandlers(
  removeMethod("matches", signature("Book", "ANY")),
  warning = \(w) {
    cat("warning:", conditionMessage(w), "\n")
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
#> warning: no method found for function ‘matches’ and signature "Book", "ANY"
#> [1] FALSE
removeClass("Shelf")
#> [1] TRUE
isClass("Shelf")
#> [1] FALSE

Source: R documentation: removeMethod

S4 pitfalls collected

The first group is about what S4 objects are not. They are not lists, so $, [ and [[ are not defined, and arithmetic, as.character(), cat() and paste() have no meaning for them until a method gives them one; length() of a plain S4 object is 1; c(b, b) makes a list. S4 objects have value semantics: assignment copies and b2@year <- 1L does not change b, unlike the Reference Class and R6 objects of Reference Classes and R6. The messages are the real ones of R 4.6.1.

setClass("Book", slots = c(title = "character", year = "integer"))
b <- new("Book", title = "Loud Roofs", year = 2021L)
msg <- \(expr) tryCatch(expr, error = \(e) conditionMessage(e))

# S4 objects are not lists: the usual operators say so.
msg(b$title)
#> [1] "$ operator not defined for this S4 class"
msg(b[1])
#> [1] "object of type 'S4' is not subsettable"
msg(b[["title"]])
#> [1] "this S4 class is not subsettable"
msg(b + 1)
#> [1] "non-numeric argument to binary operator"
msg(as.character(b))
#> [1] "no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector"
msg(cat(b))
#> [1] "argument 1 (type 'S4') cannot be handled by 'cat'"
length(b)
#> [1] 1
class(c(b, b))
#> [1] "list"

# Assignment copies: S4 objects have value semantics, like vectors.
b2 <- b
b2@year <- 1L
b@year
#> [1] 2021

Source: R documentation: Classes_Details

The second group is about initialize(). A method for initialize() is called for an empty object during conversion and validation, so it must work when called with only .Object. The method below insists on title, a mistake that works until the class gets a subclass: the validity check of StrictSub converts the object to Strict (the code of validObject() calls as(object, superClass)), which builds an empty Strict through initialize(), and the failure is reported as argument "title" is missing, with no default from a call that looks unrelated to the method. The fix is the pattern of the earlier chunk: inspect what was supplied and act on it.

# An initialize() method that insists on an argument breaks new("Book") and,
# with it, everything that builds an empty object first: here the validity
# check of a subclass, which converts the object to its superclass.
setClass("Strict",
  slots = c(title = "character"),
  validity = function(object) {
    if (length(object@title) == 1L && nzchar(object@title)) TRUE else "no title"
  }
)
# nolint start: object_name_linter.
setMethod("initialize", "Strict", function(.Object, ..., title) {
  callNextMethod(.Object, ..., title = trimws(title))
})
# nolint end
msg(new("Strict"))
#> [1] "argument \"title\" is missing, with no default"
setClass("StrictSub", contains = "Strict", slots = c(note = "character"))
msg(new("StrictSub", title = "a", note = "n"))
#> [1] "argument \"title\" is missing, with no default"

Source: R documentation: new and initialize

The third group is evaluation. All the arguments in the signature of a generic are evaluated before dispatch, even those a method does not use; arguments outside the signature keep the lazy evaluation of ordinary functions (see Lazy Evaluation and Promises). The effect is visible in the second argument of a generic: until a method mentions it in a signature the argument is inactive and stays lazy (the help page says trailing arguments are inactive until a method uses them), and the moment a method does, the argument is evaluated, with the message error in evaluating the argument 'y' in selecting a method for function 'lazy': y was evaluated. setGeneric(..., signature = "x") keeps y lazy for good, which matters for generics with arguments that are used symbolically, such as the expression of with().

# Arguments in the signature of a generic are evaluated before dispatch, even
# if the method never looks at them; arguments outside the signature stay lazy.
setGeneric("lazy", function(x, y) standardGeneric("lazy"))
#> [1] "lazy"
setMethod("lazy", "Book", function(x, y) "one-argument method ran")
msg(lazy(b, stop("y was evaluated")))
#> [1] "one-argument method ran"
setMethod("lazy", signature("Book", "numeric"), function(x, y) "two arguments")
msg(lazy(b, stop("y was evaluated")))
#> [1] "error in evaluating the argument 'y' in selecting a method for function 'lazy': y was evaluated"

setGeneric("lazy_x", function(x, y) standardGeneric("lazy_x"), signature = "x")
#> [1] "lazy_x"
setMethod("lazy_x", "Book", function(x, y) "y was never evaluated")
msg(lazy_x(b, stop("y was evaluated")))
#> [1] "y was never evaluated"

Source: R documentation: Methods_Details, How Methods Work

The last group is valueClass. A generic can declare the class of its result, and the check is real, but it adds a requirement that every method written later must satisfy; most code leaves it out.

# valueClass= checks the class of the result, which is rarely worth it.
setGeneric(
  "n_chars", function(x) standardGeneric("n_chars"),
  valueClass = "numeric"
)
#> [1] "n_chars"
setMethod("n_chars", "Book", function(x) as.character(nchar(x@title)))
msg(n_chars(b))
#> [1] "invalid value from generic function ‘n_chars’, class “character”, expected “numeric”"

Source: R documentation: setGeneric, valueClass

Other traps, in the form of a short list:

  • Redefining a class with setClass() replaces the definition silently and keeps the methods, but an object created before the change does not have the new slots: in a test, setClass("A", slots = c(x = "numeric")), then a <- new("A", x = 1), then a second setClass("A", slots = c(x = "numeric", y = "character")) makes validObject(a) fail with slots in class definition but not in object: "y". Re-create the objects after changing a class in an interactive session.

  • A class that contains = "numeric" (or another basic type) has the type of that class, typeof() is no longer "S4" and the object participates in the arithmetic of the type; a class can contain at most one basic type.

  • The slot names class and Class are not allowed, and names that begin with a dot have special meanings, so slot names should start with a letter.

  • A generic function is identified by its name and the package it belongs to (?Methods_Details). Two packages that each call setGeneric() with the same name but for different base functions define two unrelated generics, which is how clashes between packages appear; in a package the generic of another package is imported and its methods are added, not redefined (see the next section).

  • slot<- with check = FALSE can build objects that violate their class; validObject() is the audit.

  • R FAQ 8.5 is the only entry of the FAQ that is about S4.

S4 in packages

Most S4 code lives in packages, and most package problems with S4 are NAMESPACE problems. Writing R Extensions, section 1.5.6 "Namespaces with S4 classes and methods", is the authority. This section follows it, and a cut-down version of the Book model was turned into a small package (a shelfS4 package with Book, AudioBook, a generic and a show method, installed into a temporary library and loaded) to check the directives and the error messages on R 4.6.1.

DESCRIPTION: methods and Collate

The manual says that a package using formal classes and methods "should have" Depends: methods in its DESCRIPTION, together with import(methods) or importFrom(methods, ...) in the NAMESPACE; a footnote adds that Imports: methods may suffice but that package code is little exercised without the methods package on the search path and may not be fully robust to that. The NEWS agrees with both halves: R 4.4.0 made the methods package "more robust to not being attached" and made R CMD check note S4-style exports without a strong dependence on it, and R 4.5.0 changed an internal function of methods to use requireNamespace() instead of require(), so loading class definitions no longer attaches packages. The roxygen2 example below uses Imports: methods and @import methods, which is what the check package for this page used and installed without complaint; the manual’s Depends form is the conservative choice.

Class definitions are evaluated in the order of the files in R/, which is alphabetical by default, and a class must exist when a subclass, a slot or a method refers to it. That is what the Collate field of DESCRIPTION controls ("a Collate field can be used for controlling the collation order" says Writing R Extensions). A package that puts AudioBook in audiobook.R and Book in book.R is collated audiobook.R first and fails to install with the real message below; the cure is to list the files in dependency order. roxygen2 writes the field itself from @include tags (the roxygen2 section below shows it).

Package: shelfS4
Title: S4 Classes for a Library Shelf
Version: 0.0.1
Description: Book, AudioBook and Shelf classes with validity checking and
    show methods.
License: MIT + file LICENSE
Encoding: UTF-8
Imports: methods
Collate:
    'book.R'
    'audiobook.R'
    'shelf.R'

Source: Writing R Extensions: Namespaces with S4 classes and methods

With Collate: 'audiobook.R' 'book.R' in the same package, R CMD INSTALL stops while it prepares the package code for lazy loading, and the output ends with these lines (the temporary paths are left out):

** byte-compile and prepare package for lazy loading
Error in reconcilePropertiesAndPrototype(name, slots, prototype, superClasses,  :
  no definition was found for superclass “Book” in the specification of class “AudioBook”
Error: unable to load R code in package ‘shelfS4’
Execution halted
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package ‘shelfS4’

Source: Writing R Extensions: The DESCRIPTION file

The same applies to files that define methods for a generic defined in another file: the generic has to come first. In a package with several files, a layout that many S4 packages use is AllClasses.R (every setClass() and setValidity()), AllGenerics.R (every setGeneric()), then one file of methods per class, with a Collate: field listing them in that order.

NAMESPACE directives

The NAMESPACE is where S4 differs most from plain packages, because classes and methods are not functions that export() can name. The directives from section 1.5.6 are:

Directive What it does

import(methods) or importFrom(methods, ...)

Makes the methods functions available to the package code; required by R CMD check for any package that uses S4.

exportClasses(Book, AudioBook)

Exports the class definitions. Every class used outside the package must be listed; exportClassPattern() exports by regular expression (and defaults to the same pattern as exportPattern()).

exportMethods(show, pages_per_year)

Exports the methods the package defines for the named generics. Exporting the methods of a generic from the package also exports the generic when the package owns it; exporting a generic exports its methods.

export(Book, pages_per_year)

Exports ordinary objects: the constructor function and a generic that the package defines itself (this is "more natural" for a local generic, and required for an implicit generic created without any methods).

importClassesFrom(pkg, ...)

Imports named classes of another package when the whole namespace is not imported.

importMethodsFrom(pkg, ...)

Imports the generics, and their methods, of another package for the named functions.

Source: Writing R Extensions: Namespaces with S4 classes and methods

A NAMESPACE for the model is short. exportMethods(show) exports the show method for Book and AudioBook, and the manual’s remark that importMethodsFrom() also imports any generics defined in that namespace for the methods is what makes importMethodsFrom(shelfS4, pages_per_year) enough for a package that only extends the generic.

import(methods)
export(Book, pages_per_year)
exportClasses(Book, AudioBook, Shelf)
exportMethods(show, pages_per_year, length, summary)

Source: Writing R Extensions: Namespaces with S4 classes and methods

Two points are easy to miss. A generic from another package should be imported and extended, not redefined: the manual advises using the generics that stats4 exports (coef, vcov, …​) in preference to importing coef from stats and creating a second generic, because "this enables multiple packages to unambiguously set methods on those generics". And methods for primitive functions (length, [[, +) are always exported by the machinery whether or not they appear in exportMethods(), as the R Internals manual says ("Methods for primitives which are internally S4 generic are always exported"), so the line for length above is for clarity.

R 4.1.0 made R CMD check warn when a package exports an S4 class or method that does not exist, and R 4.4.0 added the note about the dependence on methods already mentioned. A package whose tests pass can still be missing a class from exportClasses(), so the check that matters is loading it in a fresh session and trying new() on each class that is meant to be public (the model was loaded and checked this way).

roxygen2

roxygen2 generates all of this from comments (see its article "Documenting S4" for the full list of supported calls; it points out that, unlike S3 and S7 methods, all S4 methods must be documented). @slot name description documents a slot in the class’s help page, @export before setClass() writes exportClasses() and before setMethod() writes exportMethods(), @export before setGeneric() writes export(), @exportClass, @exportMethod, @importClassesFrom and @importMethodsFrom are the explicit forms, and @include other.R writes the Collate field. @import methods in a package-level block writes import(methods). The documentation of S4 classes follows the topic naming of the Rd conventions (Book-class for a class, show,Book-method for a method), so class?Book and methods?show find it. roxygen2 8.1.1, which wrote the files below in the check package, records its version in Config/roxygen2/version.

#' A book on the shelf
#'
#' @slot title Title, a character string of length one.
#' @slot year Year of publication, an integer of length one.
#' @slot pages Number of pages, an integer of length one.
#' @export
setClass("Book", slots = c(title = "character", year = "integer",
                           pages = "integer"))

#' Pages per year
#'
#' @param x An object.
#' @param ... Passed to methods.
#' @return A number.
#' @export
setGeneric("pages_per_year", function(x, ...) standardGeneric("pages_per_year"))

#' @rdname pages_per_year
#' @export
setMethod("pages_per_year", "Book", function(x, ...) {
  x@pages / max(2026L - x@year, 1L)
})

#' @include book.R
NULL

#' An audio book
#' @slot minutes Running time in minutes.
#' @export
setClass("AudioBook", contains = "Book", slots = c(minutes = "integer"))

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Documenting S4

The generated NAMESPACE (with the @import methods block in R/shelfS4-package.R) and the Collate: field that @include produced were these. The Collate: field lists book.R before audiobook.R because of the @include book.R tag, and the package-level file comes last.

# Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand

export(Book)
export(pages_per_year)
exportClasses(AudioBook)
exportClasses(Book)
exportMethods(pages_per_year)
exportMethods(show)
import(methods)

Collate:
    'book.R'
    'audiobook.R'
    'shelfS4-package.R'

Source: roxygen2 package documentation: Managing imports and exports

Documenting S4 classes and methods for R CMD check follows the conventions of Writing R Extensions section 2.1.3: an \alias of the form class-class for a class and generic,signature_list-method for a method (with ANY for unspecified arguments), \S4method{generic}{signature}(arguments) in a \usage section when a method’s usage needs to be spelled out, and promptClass() and promptMethods() to generate skeletons. A package with methods for functions defined elsewhere is responsible for documenting its methods but not the function or its default method.

Rscript, scripts and the methods package

Scripts run with Rscript have methods attached (since R 3.5.0, see the start of the page), so setClass() works without library(methods). When methods is not attached, as with --default-packages=base or with R_SCRIPT_LEGACY=yes set, the functions are not found by name, and the call has to go through the namespace: methods::setClass() works but new() and isVirtualClass() need the prefix too. Neither the commands nor the failures are specific to S4, but they are the first thing to check when a script fails with could not find function "setClass". The commands and outputs below were run on R 4.6.1.

Rscript -e 'cat("package:methods" %in% search(), "\n")'
# TRUE
R_SCRIPT_LEGACY=yes Rscript -e 'cat("package:methods" %in% search(), "\n")'
# FALSE
Rscript --default-packages=base -e 'setClass("A", slots = c(x = "numeric"))'
# Error in setClass("A", slots = c(x = "numeric")) :
#   could not find function "setClass"
# Execution halted
Rscript --default-packages=base -e 'methods::setClass("A", slots = c(x = "numeric")); new("A", x = 1)'
# Error in new("A", x = 1) : could not find function "new"
# Execution halted

Source: R documentation: Rscript

The option --default-packages, the environment variable R_SCRIPT_DEFAULT_PACKAGES and the environment variable R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES choose the packages loaded at start-up, in that order of precedence. The NEWS of R 4.4.0 and 4.5.0 made the machinery that finds class definitions less dependent on methods being on the search path, but a script that calls new() or setClass() by their short names still needs it attached. A script run by Rscript therefore needs no library(methods) line.

Bioconductor and the Matrix package

S4 is the system of the Bioconductor project (https://bioconductor.org/). Its core data structures are S4 classes, among them the packages S4Vectors (low-level classes for vector-like and table-like data that other packages build on), GenomicRanges (ranges on a genome) and SummarizedExperiment (a matrix of assays with row and column annotations). The style of those packages is the one of this page: a constructor function named like the class, accessor generics instead of direct slot access, validity methods and show methods. Reading their source is a good source of idioms; the packages of CRAN and the tidyverse that do not use S4 are equally valid R, and the choice of system is the subject of OOP Overview and Base Types.

The recommended package Matrix (version 1.7-5 ships with R 4.6.1) is the most widely used S4 package of the base distribution. Matrix::Matrix() returns an object of a class chosen from a hierarchy of virtual classes (Matrix, sparseMatrix, …​) and concrete ones such as dgCMatrix, a sparse double matrix in compressed column format, and the usual S4 tools apply to it. The script builds a 0/1 matrix of which member borrowed which book from the loans table and then asks it the class questions of this page. isVirtualClass("Matrix") is TRUE, is() follows the hierarchy (a dgCMatrix is a sparseMatrix is a Matrix), and slotNames("dgCMatrix") lists the compressed-column representation (i, p, x, Dim, Dimnames, factors).

# Matrix ships with R as a recommended package and is written with S4 classes.
library(Matrix)
packageVersion("Matrix") >= "1.7.0"
#> [1] TRUE

# Which books were borrowed by which member? A sparse 0/1 matrix.
source("scenario.R")
complete <- nzchar(loans$member) & nchar(loans$isbn) == 13L
pairs <- unique(loans[complete, c("member", "isbn")])
pairs$member <- trimws(tolower(pairs$member))
pairs <- unique(pairs)
members <- sort(unique(pairs$member))
isbns <- sort(unique(pairs$isbn))
borrowed <- sparseMatrix(
  i = match(pairs$member, members), j = match(pairs$isbn, isbns),
  x = 1, dimnames = list(members, isbns)
)
dim(borrowed)
#> [1]  8 15
class(borrowed)
#> [1] "dgCMatrix"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "Matrix"
isS4(borrowed)
#> [1] TRUE
is(borrowed, "sparseMatrix")
#> [1] TRUE
is(borrowed, "Matrix")
#> [1] TRUE
isVirtualClass("Matrix")
#> [1] TRUE
isVirtualClass("sparseMatrix")
#> [1] TRUE
isVirtualClass("dgCMatrix")
#> [1] FALSE
slotNames("dgCMatrix")
#> [1] "i"        "p"        "Dim"      "Dimnames" "x"        "factors"
length(borrowed@x) == sum(borrowed != 0)
#> [1] TRUE

Source: Matrix package documentation: Matrix-class

A worked example: stats4::mle()

The stats4 package ships with R and is the smallest complete example of S4 in the standard distribution: it defines classes (mle, summary.mle, profile.mle), a constructor function (mle()) and S4 methods for generics such as coef, vcov, logLik, confint, update and profile (from stats), summary (from base) and show (from methods). Its NAMESPACE is the one that Writing R Extensions quotes in section 1.5.6, so the package-side rules of the previous section can be read in a real package. The example fits a model to the shelf scenario’s loan durations. The loans that were returned have a number of days out between loan and return; the model assumes the durations are normally distributed, and the maximum likelihood estimates of the mean and the standard deviation are the sample mean and the standard deviation with divisor n. (The Poisson model would be the natural choice for a count of days, but the data are overdispersed, the variance of the durations being about three and a half times their mean, so the normal model is the better demonstration.)

mle(minuslogl, start, method, lower, upper, nobs, ...) takes the negative log-likelihood as a function whose arguments are the parameters; their defaults serve as the start values when start is missing (the help page says so), and the optimiser is optim(), with method = "L-BFGS-B" when bounds are given. The covariance matrix is the inverse of the Hessian at the optimum. The standard deviation must stay positive, so the fit uses a lower bound of 0.01 for sigma and -Inf for mu, and nobs is passed so that BIC() and nobs() work. The estimates from the optimiser agree with the closed form to the precision shown after round(); the script rounds every printed number because the last digits of an iterative optimiser may differ between platforms.

source("scenario.R")
library(stats4)

# How long were the returned books out? One count of days per loan.
returned <- loans[!is.na(loans$return_date) & !is.na(loans$loan_date), ]
days <- as.integer(returned$return_date - returned$loan_date)
days <- days[days >= 0L]
length(days)
#> [1] 51
round(c(mean = mean(days), sd = sd(days)), 3)
#>   mean     sd
#> 20.333  8.585

# The negative log-likelihood of a normal model for the number of days.
nll <- function(mu = 20, sigma = 8) {
  -sum(dnorm(days, mean = mu, sd = sigma, log = TRUE))
}
fit <- mle(nll, method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(-Inf, 0.01), nobs = length(days))

Source: R documentation: mle

The object is an instance of an S4 class defined in stats4, isS4() is TRUE, and the class is not virtual. is(fit) is just "mle" (it extends nothing). getSlots("mle") shows what the fit keeps: the call, the estimated and full coefficient vectors, the fixed parameters, the covariance matrix, the minimum of the negative log-likelihood, the optimiser’s details, the function itself, nobs and the method. The summary has its own class, summary.mle, with three slots.

# The result is an S4 object of a class defined in stats4.
class(fit)
#> [1] "mle"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "stats4"
isS4(fit)
#> [1] TRUE
isVirtualClass("mle")
#> [1] FALSE
is(fit)
#> [1] "mle"
getSlots("mle")
#>        call        coef    fullcoef       fixed        vcov         min
#>  "language"   "numeric"   "numeric"   "numeric"    "matrix"   "numeric"
#>     details   minuslogl        nobs      method
#>      "list"  "function"   "integer" "character"
slotNames("summary.mle")
#> [1] "call"   "coef"   "m2logL"

Source: R documentation: mle-class

coef(), vcov(), logLik(), AIC(), BIC() and nobs() all work on the fit. The first three are methods of S4 generics created from stats functions and exported by stats4; AIC() and BIC() are stats generics whose default methods use logLik() and nobs(). R 4.6.0 changed those default methods to check whether the methods namespace is loaded rather than whether stats4 is, with the NEWS adding that they still use stats4::logLik and stats4::nobs and that packages no longer need to load stats4 explicitly; the same release made confint.default() work on S4 objects as long as suitable coef() and vcov() methods exist. The estimate and the closed form agree: the mean 20.33 and the divide-by-n deviation 8.5. The covariance matrix is diagonal for a normal model, with the variance of the mean estimated by sigma^2 / n (1.417 in the output) and that of the deviation by sigma^2 / (2 * n) (0.708).

# coef(), vcov(), logLik(), AIC(), BIC() and nobs() are generics with methods
# for "mle"; the estimates are the sample mean and the divide-by-n deviation.
round(coef(fit), 2)
#>    mu sigma
#> 20.33  8.50
round(sqrt(mean((days - mean(days))^2)), 2)
#> [1] 8.5
round(vcov(fit), 3)
#>          mu sigma
#> mu    1.417 0.000
#> sigma 0.000 0.708
round(logLik(fit), 2)
#> 'log Lik.' -181.51 (df=2)
round(AIC(fit), 2)
#> [1] 367.03
nobs(fit)
#> [1] 51

Source: R documentation: AIC and BIC

summary() is a method too: it returns a summary.mle object whose slots are the coefficient table with standard errors and the deviance (-2 log L, slot m2logL).

# summary() has a method too and returns an object of class summary.mle.
s <- summary(fit)
class(s)
#> [1] "summary.mle"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "stats4"
round(s@coef, 2)
#>       Estimate Std. Error
#> mu       20.33       1.19
#> sigma     8.50       0.84
round(s@m2logL, 2)
#> [1] 363.03

Source: R documentation: summary-methods

The generics belong to stats; the methods belong to stats4. showMethods("coef") lists the signatures, including the "mle" and "summary.mle" methods that stats4 registered, and existsMethod() confirms the methods for "mle". This is the structure that the package section described: a package extends a generic it does not own with exportMethods(coef) and imports the generic it uses.

# The generics come from stats; stats4 adds the methods.
showMethods("coef")
#> Function: coef (package stats)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="mle"
#> object="summary.mle"
#>
isGeneric("coef")
#> [1] TRUE
existsMethod("coef", "mle")
#> [1] TRUE
existsMethod("vcov", "mle")
#> [1] TRUE

Source: R documentation: coef-methods

Last, confint() profiles the likelihood (it computes the profile with profile() and prints a message while it works) and returns 95 percent intervals. The interval for mu is close to the Wald interval that vcov() implies, and the one for sigma is visibly asymmetric, because the profile does not assume symmetry. The call is rounded to one decimal for the same reason as the others.

# confint() profiles the likelihood and reports its progress as a message.
round(confint(fit), 1)
#> Profiling...
#>       2.5 % 97.5 %
#> mu     18.0   22.7
#> sigma   7.1   10.5

Source: R documentation: confint-methods

Version notes

The changes below were found in the NEWS files of the R releases (the 3.x entries in the separate NEWS.3 file, the 4.x ones in the release NEWS) and, where it is stated, checked against R 4.6.1.

Version Change Source

R 3.0.0

setClass() gets the slots argument, "clearer and less ambiguous" than representation; the help pages now list representation, access, version and S3methods as deprecated.

NEWS 3.0.0, ?setClass

R 3.5.0

Rscript uses the same default packages as R, so methods is attached; R_SCRIPT_LEGACY=yes restores the old behaviour (checked: still honoured by 4.6.1).

NEWS 3.5.0

R 4.0.0

The plot() generic moves to base; packages that define S4 generics for plot() must be re-installed.

NEWS 4.0.0

R 4.1.0

R CMD check warns when a package exports S4 classes or methods that do not exist; show() of a hidden S4 generic prints better.

NEWS 4.1.0

R 4.2.0

setAs() finds the right class when several packages define a class with the same name.

NEWS 4.2.0

R 4.3.3

Arguments are forwarded correctly to methods of S4 generics with ... in the middle of the formal arguments.

NEWS 4.3.3

R 4.4.0

The internal type S4SXP is renamed OBJSXP, to allow other object systems; typeof() of an S4 object is still "S4" (checked on 4.6.1), and "object" for an OBJSXP object without the S4 bit, as S7 objects are. sort() and zapsmall() become implicit S4 generics. The error for a failed S4 dispatch names the signature arguments. R CMD check notes S4-style exports without a strong dependence on methods. The methods package is more robust when it is not attached.

NEWS 4.4.0

R 4.5.0

The deprecated MethodsList functions and the "MethodsList" class are removed from methods. debug() and debugonce() accept a string naming an S4 generic. .requirePackage() no longer attaches packages.

NEWS 4.5.0

R 4.6.0

The default AIC() and BIC() methods check for the methods namespace instead of stats4; confint.default() works on S4 objects with coef() and vcov() methods; the S4 method for norm(<ANY>, type = <missing>) uses type = "O".

NEWS 4.6.0

R 4.6.1

as() coerces S4 objects to S4 superclasses that extend old-style classes correctly, instead of returning only the S3 part.

NEWS 4.6.1

Source: R NEWS: Changes in R 4.0.0 to 4.6.1

The 3.x entries are in the NEWS.3 file. The detail that surprises readers who have seen "object" in discussions of R 4.4.0 is the typeof() row: the renaming of the C type did not change what typeof() reports for a classical S4 object, and the checked value on R 4.6.1 is "S4" (see the data part section above for the script). Compose(), Funcall() and Partial() of R-devel have nothing to do with S4 and are not used here.

Where older tutorials differ

Many S4 tutorials were written for R 2.x or 3.x, and the code still runs, which is how their habits survive.

Older tutorial Current practice Why Version

setClass("Book", representation(title = "character"))

setClass("Book", slots = c(title = "character")) and contains =

slots is clearer and representation() is listed as deprecated in ?setClass

R 3.0.0

setClass(...) return value ignored, and new("Book", ...) in every call

Book <- setClass(...) and Book(...), or a hand-written constructor function

the generator records the package of the class and reads better; a constructor is the place for defaults and conversion

?setClass, value

Reading and writing slots with @ everywhere

Accessor generics and replacement generics (isbn(x), isbn(x) <- value) for the public interface

@<- checks the class of the value and nothing else; an accessor can validate and normalise

always

A print method (print.Book or setMethod("print", "Book", ...)) to control how an object displays

setMethod("show", "Book", ...)

the autoprinter of an S4 object calls show(); print() of an S4 object calls it too

always

library(methods) at the top of every script

nothing

Rscript attaches methods since R 3.5.0 (earlier Rscript did not, which is where the habit comes from)

R 3.5.0

Expecting validity to run on every assignment

Call validObject() after changes made with @<-, or assign through an accessor that does

validity runs only in initialize() and in validObject()

always

setGeneric("area", function(shape) standardGeneric("area"), valueClass = "numeric")

setGeneric("area", function(shape) standardGeneric("area"))

valueClass adds an error for methods that return another class and little else

always

prototype = prototype(...) and validity = for everything

an initialize() method and a separate setValidity() call

the setClass() help page recommends both for flexibility and clarity

?setClass

A method that insists on all its arguments in initialize()

a method that accepts being called with none

R builds empty objects when it converts or validates

always

Declaring everything an S4 class "to be safe"

Use S4 where multiple dispatch or formal validation earns its keep; S3, Reference Classes, R6 or S7 elsewhere

see the comparison in OOP Overview and Base Types

always

Source: R documentation: setClass

The rows about representation() and Rscript are the ones that cause confusion in practice, because old code works and the new text looks different.
